textbookText: Worker bees start life as cleaners and nurses, then become comb-builders and guards, and finally end their lives as foragers. This age-based division of labor ensures the smooth functioning and survival of the entire colony. 6. Write any four advantages of honey bee. Ans:- Four advantages of honey bee are as follows: i) Honey production – Honey bees produce honey, which is a nutritious food and has medicinal value. ii) Pollination – They help in pollinating crops and wild plants, which increases agricultural yield and maintains biodiversity. iii) Wax production – Beeswax obtained from honey bees is used in making candles, cosmetics, polishes, and medicines. iv) Royal jelly and propolis – These products of bees are used in medicine and health supplements for their nutritional and healing properties. 7. Mention any four characteristics of worker bee. Ans:- Four characteristics of worker bee are i) Worker bee is the smallest member of the colony and is a sterile female. ii) It has chewing and lapping type mouthparts adapted for collecting nectar and pollen. iii) The hind legs are modified with a pollen basket (corbicula) for carrying pollen. iv) The abdomen bears wax glands and a sting, useful for comb building and defense. 8. Mention any four practical knowledge which can be learned by human society from honey bee. Ans:- Four practical knowledge which can be learned by human society from honey bee are i) Division of labor – Worker bees perform tasks according to age and ability, teaching humans the importance of organized teamwork. ii) Discipline and cooperation – Bees live in a colony with strict order and coordination, showing the value of discipline in society. iii) Hard work and productivity – Bees are continuously active in collecting nectar, building combs, and caring for the hive, inspiring humans to work diligently. iv) Saving for the future – Bees store honey and pollen for future use, teaching humans the importance of planning and saving resources. 9. Identity the type of honey bee shown by 'A' in the given diagram. Write the relation between the number of such bee and the production of honey. Mention any two ways to collect excess amount of honey from apiculture. Ans:- The honey bee shown by ‘A’ in the diagram is a Worker bee. Relation with honey production: Worker bees are the main honey-gathering members of the colony. The greater the number of worker bees in a hive, the higher the production of honey, because they collect nectar, process it into honey, and store it in comb cells. Two ways to collect excess honey from apiculture: i) By maintaining strong and healthy colonies with a large number of worker bees. ii) By using improved beehives and proper management techniques, such as providing sufficient flowers or crops for nectar and controlling diseases. 10. a) Write the name of A? In what two aspects A is different from C? Ans:- The name of A is drone bee. In following two aspects A (drone bee) is different from C (worker bee). i) Reproduction: Drone is male and fertile, while worker is female and sterile.
